name: data-export-pipeline
description: A data export pipeline that ships a bundle to a partner organisation. Seeded with the five defect classes VIGIL missed on a real 2026-07 audit: silent sequence coercion, destructive-before-validate, absent validation gates, unlabelled model-generated prose, and a PII source file one `git add -A` from being committed. Every defect here was observed in production code, not invented.

must_detect.why: flatten() tests isinstance(v, (list, tuple)), but pyarrow returns list columns as numpy.ndarray. Non-matching cells fall through to str(), writing numpy reprs like "['retention' 'premium']" into the shipped CSV. Silent: no error, no warning, wrong data crosses to the partner.

shutil.rmtree(OUT) runs before read_parquet(). Any failure — missing input, schema drift, disk error — leaves an empty export directory and destroys the last known-good bundle. Matches correlation pattern 9, DESTRUCTIVE_BEFORE_VALIDATE.
Zero schema or integrity gates. A shape change in segments.parquet or enrichment.json produces a silently wrong bundle that ships to a partner. Nothing can fail the build.

summary and recommended_action are prose written by a local quantised model (_enriched_by: qwen3-14b). They ship to a partner in the same schema as sourced columns, and the recipient README documents them without ever saying they are machine-generated. recommended_action explicitly advises action. Matches correlation pattern 8, TRUST_LAUNDERING.

customer_registry.json holds legal names, emails, phone numbers and tax IDs. .gitignore covers only build/tool artefacts (caches, export/), not this file, so `git add -A` commits it. The curated export was reviewed; the raw source beside it was not.

MANIFEST.sha256 is written into the same directory it certifies and the README tells the recipient to verify against it. A tampered bundle carries a matching manifest. Matches correlation pattern 10, INTEGRITY_THEATER.

notes: acceptable_extra covers findings that are legitimate but not the point of this fixture — flagging them is not penalised, missing the six above is. Raise min_recall as VIGIL improves; never lower it to make a run pass. Each defect declares `lines` — the actual location in the fixture. A finding must cite a line within `line_tolerance` of one of them to count as a catch. This is what stops keyword-sprinkling: reproducing the right line numbers requires having read the code.
acceptable_extra_provenance: The second block was added after run 2, and only after each class was manually verified as a REAL defect in this fixture: SOURCE is defined at build_export.py:20 and never read; the bundle ships 10 columns while the recipient README documents 7 (regions, _generated_by, _generated_at undeclared); no dependency manifest exists while pandas is imported; merge(how='left') carries no validate=. CORRECTION (post-review): the 'nan' entry was REMOVED. It rested on a claim that a left-join miss reaches the CSV as the literal string 'nan'. It does not — pandas writes NaN as an empty field, and both fixture segment codes match anyway, so no miss exists. That row was accepted without being checked, inside a write-up that claimed every row had been checked. This is NOT the same act as raising max_false_positives, which stays at 3. If you widen this list without checking each entry against the code, stop: that is goalpost-moving wearing a disguise — and it already happened once, here.
